The constants are not in config and not validated; per-locus and per-delta multiplicity inflate the chance of a spurious CIS-cand.
all_findings.evidence: 34:149 `cis_spec = (pcis is not None and pcis < 0.05 and abs(dcis) > 1.8 * abs(ddr) + 0.02)`; 34:118-119 `def wp(x, y): try: return round(float(stats.wilcoxon(x, y).pvalue), 4)`. No FDR across `for spos in D` (130).
all_findings.effect_hypothesis: Which control loci pass CIS-cand is sensitive to the 1.8/+0.02 choice and to the uncorrected p threshold; the BRCA2 'two-axis cis-cand' claim could flip under a defensible alternative threshold or FDR.
all_findings.quantification_method: Sweep the 1.8 multiplier and 0.02 offset (e.g. 1.5–2.5, 0.0–0.05) and recount CIS-cand loci; apply BH-FDR over the per-locus p_cis. Report verdict stability in control_cohesion_cistest.json.
all_findings.fix_direction: Move 1.8/0.02 to a documented config with a stated calibration (e.g. bootstrap CI of d_cis−d_drift > 0), and report FDR-adjusted p_cis; declare cis only when the CI of (|d_cis|−|d_drift|) excludes 0.

all_findings.title: H5 AUC confound guard runs only 2 of 3 mandated checks — AF-bin + within-group OLS cannot run (AF column absent from TSV) — so the 'credible-regime' AUC claim is not fully confound-controlled
all_findings.description: The project's /auc-confound-guard protocol requires three gates (within-group OLS + AF-bin + permutation) before claiming any AUC>0.58. Script 26 runs the permutation null (58-71) and a within-coverage-bin AUC (165-172) and the n_cpg→TP confound AUC, but the code itself states AF-bin + within-group OLS are NOT runnable because asm_dualaxis_*.tsv has no AF/caller_af column. The credible-regime AUC and the 'anti-discriminative strong-ASM' framing therefore rest on coverage-only deconfounding; AF (a known driver of both ASM and TP/FP) is uncontrolled.
all_findings.why_wrong: Coverage-binning alone does not control AF; the protocol explicitly demands AF-bin. Claiming the credible-regime AUC is 'real' (or that strong-ASM is intrinsically anti-discriminative) without the AF gate leaves a known confound channel open. (The script honestly flags this, so it is a methodology gap not a hidden bug, but the downstream paper claim must not over-read the AUC.)
all_findings.evidence: 26:180-182 `"note": "...caller_af/AF column absent in TSV -> AF-bin + within-group OLS guards NOT runnable."` ; only within_coverage_bin_auc (167-172) and auc_ncpg_to_tp (163) implemented.
all_findings.effect_hypothesis: The credible-regime |Δβ|→TP AUC (and the anti-discriminative direction) could be partly AF-driven; magnitude/direction may move once AF-binned.
all_findings.quantification_method: Join caller_af onto the dual-axis TSV by (chrom,pos) from the ClairS/SEQC2 VCFs, then re-run AUC within AF bins and as within-group OLS residual of |Δβ| on AF; compare AUC and perm-p to the AF-blind values in obs26_H5_stats.json.
all_findings.fix_direction: Add AF to the TSV upstream (18_dual_axis_pivot) and complete the third guard; until then, state in the paper that the H5 AUC is coverage-controlled but AF-uncontrolled.

all_findings.title: Hardcoded analysis constants (window, MIN_N, STRONG=0.10, thresholds, ML cutoffs) duplicated across scripts with silent divergence (±600 vs ±1000 bp; MIN_N 3 vs 8) — no shared config
all_findings.description: Each script re-declares its own window / min-read / strong-ASM threshold. 03_step4 uses ±1000bp window while 57/59/49 use ±600bp; MIN_N is 3 in 18/57/59 but MIN_GROUP=8 in 49 and n<6/<3 ad hoc in 34's silhouette. STRONG=0.10 (59) vs ASM_MIN=0.05 (58) vs Cohen ribbon 0.05 elsewhere. These are paper-level analysis parameters living as per-file literals, so a change in one place silently desynchronizes the flagship Δβ window from the cross-sample window.
all_findings.why_wrong: Different window sizes change the set of CpGs averaged into beta and thus Δβ; comparing HCC1395 flagship Δβ (±1000) to cross-sample Δβ (±600) mixes window口徑. The duplicated thresholds are exactly the kind of magic constant the project rules say should be config.
all_findings.evidence: 03_step4:29 `WINDOW_BP = 1000` vs 59:44 `WINDOW = 600` vs 57:55 `WINDOW = 600`; 49:55 `MIN_GROUP = 8` vs 18:34 `MIN_PAIRED = 5` vs 57:56 `MIN_N = 3`.
all_findings.effect_hypothesis: Flagship BRCA2 Δβ (±1000) and the cross-sample/genome-wide Δβ (±600) are on slightly different window口徑; small but real shift in beta and in which CpGs count.
all_findings.quantification_method: Recompute BRCA2 Δβ at both ±600 and ±1000 bp; report sensitivity. Inventory all (WINDOW, MIN_N, STRONG) literals across scripts.
all_findings.fix_direction: Hoist window/MIN_N/STRONG/ASM_MIN into one shared config module imported by all ASM scripts; standardize the window for all paper Δβ.

all_findings.title: germline (HP1-vs-HP2 / ALLELE) Δβ is reported as ASM but is baseline-allelic-confounded by construction — synthesis labels it 'recurrent_germline_asm/imprinting' without a germline-het negative control in the number path
all_findings.description: germline_delta = beta(HP2)−beta(HP1) (57:258) is gated at |Δβ|>=0.10 and, when >=2 samples pass with concordant sign, labelled imprinting_consistent (58:150-162). Per the project's own methodology memory (feedback_asm_allele_axis_baseline_confound), the ALLELE/HP1-vs-HP2 axis cannot distinguish somatic-specific ASM from baseline het allelic methylation — only the somatic-controlled HP-axis (HP1 vs HP1-1) is clean. The synthesis does separate somatic vs germline axes (good), but it still emits a 'recurrent germline ASM / imprinting' headline from HP1-vs-HP2 without any germline-het null, and sign-concordance across samples is treated as evidence for imprinting. Sign-concordant baseline allelic methylation (not parent-of-origin imprinting) would produce the same pattern.
all_findings.why_wrong: Calling HP1-vs-HP2 recurrence 'imprinting-consistent' conflates true parent-of-origin imprinting with shared baseline allelic methylation; the only discriminator (somatic-controlled axis or a germline-het null) is not applied to the germline-axis hits. Sign-concordance is necessary but not sufficient for imprinting.
all_findings.evidence: 57:256-259 `germ_delta = round(g2['beta'] - g1['beta'], 4)`; 58:150 `imprinting_consistent = (n_germ >= 2 and sign_concordant)`. No het-null comparison; memory feedback_asm_allele_axis_baseline_confound documents ALLELE-axis confound.
all_findings.effect_hypothesis: Some 'imprinting_consistent' hits are shared baseline allelic methylation, not imprinting; the imprinting count is an upper bound. Direction (which loci) may stand but the imprinting label over-claims mechanism.
all_findings.quantification_method: For each recurrent_germline hit, compare |germline Δβ| against the per-sample germline-het |Δβ| null distribution at non-imprinted het sites (or restrict imprinting claims to the IGF2/H19/GNAS panel already in 59); recount imprinting_consistent that exceed the het null.
all_findings.fix_direction: Replace the imprinting label with 'recurrent allelic methylation' unless the locus is a known imprinted DMR (59 panel) OR exceeds a germline-het null; state the baseline-allelic confound in the paper.

verified_high.title: per-CpG Wilcoxon treats spatially-autocorrelated CpGs within a ±600/1000bp window as independent paired units → p systematically under-estimated (drives strong-ASM gate + credible-locus selection + AUC inputs)
verified_high.description: The core per-locus significance number `wilcoxon_p` is computed by `stats.wilcoxon(pg, ps)` where pg/ps are per-CpG betas of all CpGs in a ±600bp (18/57/59) or ±1000bp (03) window (paired_test:106-116). Wilcoxon signed-rank assumes the N paired differences are i.i.d. exchangeable. CpG methylation within a sub-kb window is strongly spatially autocorrelated (co-methylation blocks) AND each per-CpG beta is itself an average of correlated reads. So the effective number of independent units is far smaller than n_paired_cpg. This inflates the test statistic's significance (p too small). The same anti-conservative p then feeds: the strong-ASM Bonferroni gate (22_tp_vs_fp_stats_confirm.py:26-27 uses `wilcoxon_p < 0.05/len(d)`), the 'significant regime' AUC subset (26_H5:86,98), and the credible-loci annotation that 57/59 read back.
verified_high.why_wrong: Wilcoxon over correlated per-CpG betas violates the independence/exchangeability assumption; window-level p is anti-conservative. Any downstream count of 'significant ASM loci', the Bonferroni survivors in 22, and the 'sig' AUC stratum in 26 inherit the bias.
verified_high.evidence: 18_dual_axis_pivot.py:104-116 `def paired_test(cpgs, g_germ, g_som): pg, ps = [], []  for mpos, hpd in cpgs.items(): ... pg.append(bg); ps.append(bs)  ... w_p = float(stats.wilcoxon(pg, ps).pvalue)` — paired units = per-CpG window betas, no autocorrelation/cluster adjustment. 03_step4:157 `stats.wilcoxon(paired_g, paired_s, ...)` over per-CpG betas in ±1000bp window identically.
verified_high.effect_hypothesis: Number of loci declared 'significant ASM' (and the Bonferroni-surviving strong set) is likely inflated vs a dependency-aware test; absolute Δβ point estimates (mean_delta) are unaffected, only the p-values / significance counts shift.
verified_high.quantification_method: Re-run paired_test with a block-bootstrap or cluster-robust p (resample reads, not CpGs, or collapse co-methylated CpGs to one effective unit) on asm_dualaxis_tp.tsv / asm_dualaxis_fp.tsv; compare count of wilcoxon_p<0.05 and Bonferroni survivors (22) before vs after. Also compute the autocorrelation of per-CpG deltas within windows to estimate effective n.
verified_high.fix_direction: Report Δβ as the primary effect (already done) and treat per-CpG Wilcoxon p only as a descriptive ranking, OR replace with a read-permutation null (shuffle HP labels among reads, recompute window mean Δβ) which respects the read as the exchangeable unit. Do not gate 'significant ASM' on this p alone.

verdict.reasoning: The underlying statistical claim is technically correct but the severity and causal chain are substantially overstated. VERIFIED FACTS: (1) 18_dual_axis_pivot.py:104-126 `paired_test` does call `stats.wilcoxon(pg, ps)` where pg/ps are per-CpG window betas, with no autocorrelation/cluster adjustment (lines 110, 116). (2) 03_step4_ism_methylation_diff.py:157 has the identical pattern over per-CpG betas in a ±1000bp window. (3) CpG methylation within a sub-kb window is genuinely spatially autocorrelated, so signed-rank exchangeability is violated and the per-window p is anti-conservative in principle. The reviewer is right that this is a real methodological concern. WHY SEVERITY/CHAIN IS OVERSTATED: (a) Credible-locus selection (39_annotate_credible_loci.py, which writes credible_loci_annotation.tsv consumed by 57/59) is driven by the regime-A definition `n_cpg>=100 & extremity<=0.3 & nonLOH` (26_H5:105-112, 39:6), which is ORTHOGONAL to wilcoxon_p — contradicting the claim that the anti-conservative p drives credible-locus selection. (b) The strong-ASM gate in 32_credibility_patch.py and 22:27 pairs `wilcoxon_p<BONF` with a co-required `|mean_delta|>=0.1` effect-size threshold; an anti-conservative p that admits a trivial effect is blocked by the |Δβ| requirement, so the gate is NOT p-alone. (c) The AUC score in 26_H5 (run_set:139, score=`abs_delta`) is the effect size, not p; `wilcoxon_p<0.05` only defines one secondary stratum (`bp_all_significant_p05`, 26:150) while the headline conclusion is the regime-A `b_credible_regime` AUC (26:152,181), p-independent. (d) Critically, the team already reasons explicitly about the n-coupling of the Wilcoxon p: 32_credibility_patch.py:136-161 builds `wilcoxon_min_p(n)=2/2^n` floor and a coverage-power curve stating 'Bins where wilcoxon_floor_p_at_lo > Bonferroni alpha CANNOT reach strong-ASM' — so the p's dependence on n is understood and a very stringent Bonferroni (0.05/51091≈1e-6) is applied. NET: the autocorrelation caveat genuinely makes the `n_bonf_sig` counts and the p<0.05 stratum anti-conservative (the inflation is real), but it does not 'drive' the headline credible-locus or AUC conclusions as claimed, and the |Δβ|≥0.1 co-requirement plus stringent Bonferroni materially mitigate the practical impact. A real but mitigated and partly-misattributed confound → not HIGH.

perReviewer.area: PYTOOL — harness anti-fabrication + statistics tools (number_provenance.py, fill_report.py, harness_health.py, plot_setup.py, build_focus_board.py, A3_5features_TP_FP_analysis.py)
perReviewer.notes:
All 6 target files read in full and key behaviors verified empirically (not by inspection alone).

Highest-impact findings on the anti-fabrication line itself:
- PYTOOL-1 (HIGH): fill_report.py Layer A 'by-construction' guarantee is defeated by null/NaN data values, which render as literal 'None'/'nan' instead of refusing — the single most common real-world case (key present, value not yet computed). This is the #1 fix because it undermines the strongest of the three §13 layers.
- PYTOOL-2 (MEDIUM): gate behavior contradicts its documented FAIL-OPEN contract for the zero-sources case on validated/PI paths (verified exit 2). Needs an intent decision + doc/code reconciliation.
- PYTOOL-4/5 (MEDIUM/LOW): the Layer B gate's substring matching produces both false-negatives (fabricated number matches inside an unrelated longer number — '0.58' in '100.589') and sign-blindness (unicode-minus stripped → '+0.055' matches true '−0.055'), the latter directly relevant to this project's documented direction-reversed fabrication incidents.

Harness-self-audit blind spots (no research-number effect but they give false confidence):
- PYTOOL-3 (MEDIUM): light_queue is structurally incapable of going non-GREEN (looks for status 'queued' which never occurs; real statuses are pending/adopted/adopted_annotation). build_focus_board.py uses a correct broader LIVE set — the two tools disagree.
- PYTOOL-10 (LOW): _claim max() drift heuristic is fragile against CLAUDE.md's own historical-count changelog.

A3 statistics (G3 5-feature cross-sample analysis):
- PYTOOL-6 (MEDIUM): NG binning v<=2 mislabels NG∈{0,1} (2067 rows verified in data) as 'NG2', conflating no-subgroup loci with 2-subgroup loci — needs rerun of the 9-cell heatmap.
- PYTOOL-7 (MEDIUM): fillna(0) conflates missing Cohen's d with neutral direction, biasing the >=4/5 sign-consistency conclusion — needs rerun.
- PYTOOL-8 (LOW): 45 MWU tests, no multiple-testing correction, and MWU ignores read-level dependence (anti-conservative).
- PYTOOL-9 (LOW): AUC bar ylim(0.3,1.0) clips anti-discriminative features (AUC<0.3), relevant given documented anti-discriminative ASM (OR=0.194 in FP).

plot_setup.py: reviewed in full; no misleading axis/scale defaults (it only sets fonts/dpi, never axis limits or log scales). The font-fallback logic and fail-safe (never raise) are sound. No finding.

build_focus_board.py: reviewed in full; it correctly avoids hardcoding research metrics (verdict/tier/p all injected, '?' on missing), Layer-A consistent. Its broader LIVE set is the CORRECT reference that exposes harness_health's light_queue bug (PYTOOL-3). No independent defect found in it.

I did NOT fabricate any effect magnitudes — for findings needing rerun (PYTOOL-6, -7) I provide the exact TSV/command to quantify. Empirical checks were run via lightweight python -c using the actual repo data (hypothesis_queue.json, per_bam_master_V6.tsv) and a /tmp sandbox for the gate exit-code simulation.

all_findings.title: fill_report.py renders null/NaN data values as literal 'None'/'nan' instead of refusing — breaks the by-construction anti-fabrication guarantee (Layer A)
all_findings.description: fill_report.py is the §13 Layer A 'by-construction' renderer whose whole point (docstring lines 16-24) is that 'a fabricated number is physically impossible — you cannot type a value that is not a key in the data file', and 'if ANY placeholder is unresolved -> refuse to write'. But resolve() (line 34) only checks key PRESENCE: `part in cur`. When a key exists with value null (the project's standard 'not yet computed' placeholder, e.g. {"auc": null}) resolve returns (True, None), so it is NOT counted as missing, and fmt() (line 50) returns str(None)='None'. Verified: fmt(None)='None', fmt(nan)='nan', resolve({'auc':None},'auc')=(True,None).
all_findings.why_wrong: An un-computed/null metric silently renders the literal text 'None' (or 'nan') into a validated/PI report rather than triggering the documented refusal. The downstream gate (number_provenance) only checks 'metric-shaped' numbers, so 'None'/'nan' pass both layers undetected. The construction-level guarantee is defeated by the most common real-world case: a data.json with a key present but value not yet filled.
all_findings.evidence: line 38: `if isinstance(cur, dict) and part in cur:` (presence only) → line 47 returns (True, cur even if None); line 50-54 fmt: `if isinstance(value,(dict,list)): ...; return str(value)` → str(None)='None'. Empirical: resolve null val: (True, None); fmt(None) = 'None'.
all_findings.effect_hypothesis: Reports rendered from incomplete data.json show 'None'/'nan' in place of real metrics; reviewers may read past them or they pass the provenance gate. Direction: false sense of completeness, not a numeric direction error per se.
all_findings.quantification_method: grep -rn 'None\|nan' on any HTML/MD produced via fill_report.py under docs/reports/; or unit-test resolve() with a data.json containing null values. Count how many template keys in real metrics.json files are null.
all_findings.fix_direction: Treat resolved-but-None/NaN as missing: in resolve() or sub(), if found and val is None (or float nan) → append to missing and emit {{MISSING:key}} unless --allow-missing. Optionally also refuse on empty-string values for strict output.

all_findings.title: number_provenance gate contradicts its own FAIL-OPEN contract: zero co-located sources on a validated/PI path → exit 2 BLOCK (doc says exit 0)
all_findings.description: The module docstring (lines 17-20) states the gate is FAIL-OPEN: 'any error / no content / no sources => exit 0 (a broken hook must never block all writes)'. But cmd_gate() has no zero-sources guard. If gather_sources() returns [] (no _assets/, no data_sources: frontmatter, no sibling .json/.tsv), then every extracted metric is 'unsourced', and on a strict path is_strict_path()==True returns exit 2. Verified empirically: a validated/ report with two metrics and no co-located source files is BLOCKED (exit 2).
all_findings.why_wrong: Either the documented contract is wrong (misleads maintainers/future audits who rely on 'no sources => exit 0') or the behavior is wrong (a legitimate validated report whose numbers live in a non-adjacent file, cited inline, gets hard-blocked unless it adds an override comment). This is a real friction/correctness inconsistency in a Hard-Gate hook.
all_findings.evidence: docstring L18: 'no sources => exit 0'. Code path L191 `sources = gather_sources(...)`; L192 `unsourced = [m for m in metrics if find_token(m,sources) is None]`; L194 `strict=is_strict_path(fpath)`; L199-209 `if strict: ... return 2`. No `if not sources: return 0`. Simulation on /tmp validated/test.md (no sources) → printed BLOCK, EXIT CODE: 2.
all_findings.effect_hypothesis: Validated/PI writes with all-remote sourcing get blocked; or, if the doc reflects true intent, the gate is silently stricter than documented. Not a research-number direction error, but a governance-tool reliability issue.
all_findings.quantification_method: Grep settings.local.json to confirm gate is wired on Edit|Write *.md/*.html; replay PreToolUse JSON for any existing validated report lacking _assets to count how many would block.
all_findings.fix_direction: Decide intent: (a) if strict-should-require-sources is correct, fix the docstring to remove 'no sources => exit 0'; or (b) if fail-open is correct, add `if not sources: return 0` before the strict branch (matching the contract). Document whichever is chosen.

all_findings.title: harness_health light_queue is permanently blind: counts only status=='queued' but the real queue uses pending/adopted/adopted_annotation → always GREEN, never flags hygiene
all_findings.description: light_queue() (line 310) computes `queued = [... if str(h.get('status')).lower() == 'queued']`. The actual hypothesis_queue.json statuses (verified) are: adopted(2), rejected(7), adopted_annotation(3), closed(6), pending(5) — ZERO 'queued'. So queued always = [], the `len(queued) >= 3` branch never fires, and the light is permanently GREEN regardless of how many live/DEAD-direction hypotheses sit in the queue. build_focus_board.py uses a much broader LIVE set {pending, adopted, adopted_annotation, testing, queued, active}, so the two harness tools disagree on what 'live' means.
all_findings.why_wrong: The QUEUE HYGIENE health light gives false reassurance — it can never trigger its concluded-DEAD-direction warning because no entry ever has the literal status it looks for. A self-audit light that is structurally incapable of going non-GREEN is worse than no light (false confidence).
all_findings.evidence: L310: `... == 'queued'`. Empirical: light_queue(queue) → status GREEN, rows ['queued=0 []'], while real statuses = {adopted:2, rejected:7, adopted_annotation:3, closed:6, pending:5} (10 live). Contrast build_focus_board.py L136: `LIVE = {'pending','adopted','adopted_annotation','testing','queued','active'}`.
all_findings.effect_hypothesis: Queue bloat / lingering DEAD-direction hypotheses go undetected by /harness-health. No research-number effect; harness-self-audit blind spot.
all_findings.quantification_method: Run `python3 scripts/harness_health.py` and confirm QUEUE HYGIENE=GREEN with queued=0 despite 10 live entries; cross-check against build_focus_board.py q_live count.
all_findings.fix_direction: Align light_queue with build_focus_board's LIVE set (pending/adopted/adopted_annotation/testing/active/queued), or read the canonical 'live' definition from one shared constant. Then re-evaluate the >=3 + DEAD-keyword threshold against real data.

all_findings.title: number_provenance find_token uses bare substring match → false-negatives: fabricated metric counted as 'sourced' if it appears inside an unrelated longer number
all_findings.description: find_token (line 145) checks `if token in line` — a raw substring test with no numeric-boundary check. The docstring intentionally allows trailing-precision tolerance (report 0.866 inside source 0.8662), but the same mechanism makes a fabricated metric pass whenever it is a substring of any unrelated number anywhere in the bounded source set. Verified: '0.58' in '100.589'→True; '44' in '12445'→True; '0.50' in '10.502'→True; '0.86' in 'cov=100.860'→True; '0.99' (report) in 'p=0.999' (source)→True.
all_findings.why_wrong: The gate's job is to catch hand-typed/fabricated numbers absent from sources (Layer B backstop). Bare substring matching gives an attacker/AI an easy false-negative: any genomic coordinate, coverage value, sample size, or higher-precision metric in the source files can accidentally 'source' a fabricated value. The detection rate is silently lower than the docstring's claimed 真實 axis implies.
all_findings.evidence: L145: `if token in line:` then returns file:line. Empirical false matches: '0.58' in '100.589'→True, '44' in '12445'→True, '0.50' in '10.502'→True. (Asymmetric precision also breaks the intended case: source 0.866 vs report 0.8662 → '0.8662' in '...0.866...' = False, false NO-SOURCE.)
all_findings.effect_hypothesis: Gate under-detects fabricated metrics (more false-negatives), and occasionally over-flags when report carries MORE precision than source (false NO-SOURCE). Both reduce gate trustworthiness; direction = weaker anti-fabrication than advertised.
all_findings.quantification_method: Run audit on a sample of validated reports and manually verify a few '✅ sourced' rows actually correspond to the intended metric vs an accidental substring. Count mismatches.
all_findings.fix_direction: Match with numeric boundaries: regex `(?<![\d.])TOKEN(?![\d])` (allow trailing digits only for the documented precision-rounding case via an explicit prefix-of-source check), or normalize both sides to floats and compare with a tolerance band rather than substring.

all_findings.title: number_provenance metric extraction strips the sign of negative metrics (unicode minus and ASCII), so direction-sensitive values (Δβ, ρ) are checked sign-agnostically
all_findings.description: _P1 (line 46) has no sign group, so 'Δβ=-0.122' yields both '-0.122' and '0.122' via the two regexes but the unicode-minus case 'Δβ=−0.122' (U+2212, the form actually used across this project's memory/reports) yields only '0.122' because _P2's `[-+]?` matches ASCII only and _P1 captures the bare float. Verified: 'partial ρ=−0.055' → ['0.055']; 'Δβ=−0.122' → ['0.122'].
all_findings.why_wrong: ASM is fundamentally directional (HP1 vs HP2 hypo/hyper; ρ sign indicates confound direction). The provenance gate would treat a fabricated '+0.055' as sourced if the file contains the true '−0.055' (since both reduce to substring '0.055'). The 2026-06-01 postmortem specifically cites direction-reversed fabrications (BRCA2 true +0.866 vs fabricated values), exactly the class this sign-stripping misses.
all_findings.evidence: L46 `_P1 = r'(?<![\w.])\d+\.\d{2,}(?![\w])'` (no sign). L48-51 _P2 `([-+]?\d+...)` matches ASCII -/+ only, not U+2212. Empirical: 'partial ρ=−0.055' → ['0.055'] (sign dropped). A source with '−0.055' matches a fabricated '0.055'.
all_findings.effect_hypothesis: Sign-flipped fabrications evade the gate. Low frequency but high-stakes given the project's documented direction-reversal incidents.
all_findings.quantification_method: Search project reports for unicode-minus metrics (grep U+2212) and check whether the gate would treat a sign-flipped variant as sourced.
all_findings.fix_direction: Normalize unicode minus (U+2212/U+FF0D) to ASCII '-' before extraction, and include the sign in the token (and in find_token boundary matching) so '+0.055' and '-0.055' are distinct.

all_findings.title: A3 9-cell NG binning mislabels NG∈{0,1} as 'NG2' (v<=2), contradicting the 'NG==2' label/docstring; conflates no-subgroup loci with 2-subgroup loci
all_findings.description: ng_bin() (line 302) returns 'NG2' for all `v <= 2`, but the docstring (line 37: 'NG==2 / NG==3 / NG>=4') and the bin label NG2 (line 352) claim NG2 means exactly NG==2. Verified the data has NG=0 (53 rows) and NG=1 (2014 rows) in per_bam_master_V6.tsv, so 2067 NG∈{0,1} loci are folded into the 'NG2' bin.
all_findings.why_wrong: NG is the methylation-defined number-of-groups (the tool's core read-clustering output). NG=1 (single group) / NG=0 means NO methylation subgrouping — conceptually the opposite of NG=2 (two subgroups, the minimal ASM signal). Folding them into a bin labeled 'NG2' contaminates the 9-cell TP-rate heatmap and any NG×AF×LOH interpretation, and the figure/TSV mislead the reader about what the bin contains.
all_findings.evidence: L302-303: `if v <= 2: return 'NG2'`. Docstring L37: 'NG==2'. Data: `cut -f12 per_bam_master_V6.tsv | sort | uniq -c` → 2014×'1', 53×'0' (plus 9285×'2'). So ~2067 NG<2 rows land in 'NG2'.
all_findings.effect_hypothesis: 9-cell TP-rate per (LOH,NG2,AF) cell is diluted/biased by no-subgroup loci; could shift the apparent TP-rate of the 'NG2' bin in either direction depending on whether NG<2 loci are TP- or FP-enriched.
all_findings.quantification_method: Re-bin with strict NG==2 (and add an NG<2 bin), recompute A3_9cell_heatmap_data_5sample.tsv TP_rate per cell, and compare the 'NG2' row before/after using the existing TSV.
all_findings.fix_direction: Either fix ng_bin to `if v == 2: 'NG2'` and add an explicit NG01/NG<2 bin, or relabel the bin 'NGle2' and update docstring/figure legends to match the actual semantics.

all_findings.title: A3 cross-sample sign-consistency conflates missing-data (NaN Cohen's d) with neutral direction (sign 0), penalizing under-powered samples in the >=4/5 threshold
all_findings.description: Per-feature sign-agreement (line 234) does `signs = np.sign(ds.fillna(0).values)`. A sample whose Cohen's d is NaN (feature_stats returns NaN when n_TP<5 or n_FP<5, line 168-171, or pooled sd==0) becomes 0 after fillna(0), counted as n_zero, and dilutes sign_majority. sign_consistent requires sign_majority>=4 of 5. Verified: 3 real-positive samples + 2 NaN → majority=3 → flagged NOT consistent, even though 3/3 non-missing samples fully agree.
all_findings.why_wrong: Missing/under-powered (small-N) is not the same as 'no effect / neutral direction'. Treating NaN as a zero-sign vote against consistency biases the cross-sample direction-consistency conclusion toward 'inconsistent' precisely for features that are sparse in some samples — a systematic, not random, bias. This directly feeds the STATUS SUMMARY 'sign-consistent N/9' claim.
all_findings.evidence: L168-171 returns AUC/d=NaN when len(tp)<5 or len(fp)<5. L234 `signs = np.sign(ds.fillna(0).values)`; L237 `n_zero=int((signs==0).sum())`; L249-250 `sign_majority=max(n_pos,n_neg)`, `sign_consistent=int(sign_majority>=4)`. Empirical: signs [1,1,1,0,0] → majority 3 → not consistent.
all_findings.effect_hypothesis: Some features are under-reported as direction-inconsistent (false negatives for consistency), under-stating cross-sample reproducibility; or threshold tuning hides it. Could shift the 'N/9 sign-consistent' headline either way.
all_findings.quantification_method: Recompute sign_consistent counting only non-NaN samples (e.g., majority over non-missing, or require >=4 of the AVAILABLE samples) and diff against current cons_df from A3_direction_consistency_spearman.tsv.
all_findings.fix_direction: Drop NaN samples before sign counting (signs = np.sign(ds.dropna())), and define consistency as majority among available samples with a minimum-available-N guard, rather than fillna(0).

all_findings.title: A3 runs 45 Mann-Whitney tests (9 features × 5 samples) with no multiple-testing correction; p-values reported as-is
all_findings.description: feature_stats computes a two-sided Mann-Whitney U p-value per (sample, feature) and writes raw p to A3_per_feature_AUC_cohend_5sample.tsv. With 9 features × 5 samples = 45 tests, no FDR/Bonferroni/Holm adjustment is applied (verified: no multipletests/fdr/bonferroni in file). read-level methylation also has within-read CpG dependence and between-read dependence, so even per-test p is anti-conservative; un-adjusted family-wise it is more so.
all_findings.why_wrong: If any downstream report/decision interprets these p-values as significance across the 45-test family, the false-positive rate is inflated. The script's own STATUS SUMMARY leans on AUC ranges, but the TSV exposes raw p that could be cited as 'significant'.
all_findings.evidence: L179 `stats.mannwhitneyu(tp, fp, alternative='two-sided')`; per_feat_df written with raw 'pvalue' (L206). grep for multipletests/fdr/bonferroni → none found.
all_findings.effect_hypothesis: Over-statement of per-cell significance; direction = too many 'significant' calls if p<0.05 is applied naively across 45 tests.
all_findings.quantification_method: Apply BH-FDR to the 45 p-values in A3_per_feature_AUC_cohend_5sample.tsv and count how many cross the 0.05 threshold before vs after.
all_findings.fix_direction: Add a BH-FDR (statsmodels multipletests) column q-value to the TSV and report it; document the test family and the read-dependence caveat (MWU treats reads as independent).

all_findings.title: A3 AUC bar chart y-axis floored at 0.3 visually clips strongly anti-discriminative features (AUC<0.3), hiding the magnitude of TP<FP separation
all_findings.description: The AUC bar panel sets `axes[0].set_ylim(0.3, 1.0)` (line 419). roc_auc_score(y,x) is orientation-sensitive (line 175): a feature lower in TP than FP yields AUC<0.5, and a strongly anti-discriminative feature can approach 0. With a 0.3 floor those bars are clipped to the axis bottom, so a feature with AUC=0.05 looks identical to AUC=0.3 (both pinned at the floor). The 0.58 ceiling line is drawn but no symmetric lower reference.
all_findings.why_wrong: AUC<0.5 is meaningful (predictive in the OPPOSITE direction) and the project has documented anti-discriminative ASM signals (memory: strong-ASM enriched in FP, OR=0.194). Clipping the lower range understates anti-discriminative strength and can mislead a reader into thinking a strongly-reversed feature is merely 'near random'.
all_findings.evidence: L416-417 axhline 0.58 ceiling; L419 `axes[0].set_ylim(0.3, 1.0)`. No lower bound near 0; roc_auc_score is not abs-oriented (L175).
all_findings.effect_hypothesis: Visual under-representation of features with AUC<0.3; could cause a reviewer to overlook a strong reversed-direction signal. No effect on the underlying TSV numbers.
all_findings.quantification_method: Re-render with ylim(0,1) and inspect whether any (feature,sample) AUC falls below 0.3 in A3_per_feature_AUC_cohend_5sample.tsv (np.nanmin already computed as auc_min in STATUS SUMMARY).
all_findings.fix_direction: Set ylim(0,1) (or symmetric around 0.5) and add a lower reference line at 0.42 (mirror of 0.58); or plot |AUC-0.5| if only magnitude is intended, with a note.

all_findings.title: harness_health _claim uses max() over all regex matches for doc-claimed counts — fragile drift detection that can silently pick a stale/larger number
all_findings.description: _claim() (line 122) returns max() of all integers matched by the count pattern in CLAUDE.md. light_count compares disk count vs this max-claimed value. It happens to work today (only one SKILL.md count has a numeric prefix → 47), but the pattern `(\d+)\s*個?\s*SKILL\.md` and max() will mis-fire the moment CLAUDE.md mentions a historical count alongside the current one (e.g. '45 SKILL.md (was 44)' → picks 45) — and the COUNT DRIFT light would then read the wrong 'claimed' value and either hide or invent drift.
all_findings.why_wrong: A drift detector should compare disk truth against the single CURRENT documented count, not the maximum of every count-shaped token in a prose file that explicitly logs historical counts (CLAUDE.md §3 keeps a drift-correction changelog full of old numbers like 44/45/46/47). max() is a heuristic that defeats the detector's purpose under exactly the conditions it is meant to catch.
all_findings.evidence: L122 `return max(nums) if nums else default`. CLAUDE.md §3 contains historical counts (44, 45, 46, 47). Empirical today: skill claim parsed=47 (matches disk), but only because just one '47 SKILL.md' has a number prefix; agent uses `or 18` hardcoded fallback (L220).
all_findings.effect_hypothesis: Future false-GREEN or false-RED on the COUNT DRIFT light when CLAUDE.md logs old counts; harness-self-audit reliability. No research-number effect.
all_findings.quantification_method: Add a historical count line to a CLAUDE.md copy and run light_count to observe mis-pick; or assert the parsed claim equals the single intended current value.
all_findings.fix_direction: Anchor the count to a single canonical marker (e.g., a dedicated 'CURRENT_SKILL_COUNT: N' line) rather than max() over prose; or take the count from the first match in a known sentence, with an explicit comment.

verified_high.title: fill_report.py renders null/NaN data values as literal 'None'/'nan' instead of refusing — breaks the by-construction anti-fabrication guarantee (Layer A)
verified_high.description: fill_report.py is the §13 Layer A 'by-construction' renderer whose whole point (docstring lines 16-24) is that 'a fabricated number is physically impossible — you cannot type a value that is not a key in the data file', and 'if ANY placeholder is unresolved -> refuse to write'. But resolve() (line 34) only checks key PRESENCE: `part in cur`. When a key exists with value null (the project's standard 'not yet computed' placeholder, e.g. {"auc": null}) resolve returns (True, None), so it is NOT counted as missing, and fmt() (line 50) returns str(None)='None'. Verified: fmt(None)='None', fmt(nan)='nan', resolve({'auc':None},'auc')=(True,None).
verified_high.why_wrong: An un-computed/null metric silently renders the literal text 'None' (or 'nan') into a validated/PI report rather than triggering the documented refusal. The downstream gate (number_provenance) only checks 'metric-shaped' numbers, so 'None'/'nan' pass both layers undetected. The construction-level guarantee is defeated by the most common real-world case: a data.json with a key present but value not yet filled.
verified_high.evidence: line 38: `if isinstance(cur, dict) and part in cur:` (presence only) → line 47 returns (True, cur even if None); line 50-54 fmt: `if isinstance(value,(dict,list)): ...; return str(value)` → str(None)='None'. Empirical: resolve null val: (True, None); fmt(None) = 'None'.
verified_high.effect_hypothesis: Reports rendered from incomplete data.json show 'None'/'nan' in place of real metrics; reviewers may read past them or they pass the provenance gate. Direction: false sense of completeness, not a numeric direction error per se.
verified_high.quantification_method: grep -rn 'None\|nan' on any HTML/MD produced via fill_report.py under docs/reports/; or unit-test resolve() with a data.json containing null values. Count how many template keys in real metrics.json files are null.
verified_high.fix_direction: Treat resolved-but-None/NaN as missing: in resolve() or sub(), if found and val is None (or float nan) → append to missing and emit {{MISSING:key}} unless --allow-missing. Optionally also refuse on empty-string values for strict output.

verdict.reasoning:
All technical claims verified directly against scripts/fill_report.py and empirically. resolve() at line 38 checks key PRESENCE only (`isinstance(cur, dict) and part in cur`), so a present-but-null key returns (True, cur) at line 47 — confirmed: resolve({'auc': None}, 'auc') = (True, None). fmt() at line 54 does `return str(value)` for non-dict/list — confirmed fmt(None)='None', fmt(float('nan'))='nan'. In main(), the `missing` list (and thus the documented REFUSE at lines 93-97) is only populated when `not found` (line 80), so null/NaN values are never counted missing and the literal text 'None'/'nan' is written into output.

This violates the explicit contract. The docstring lines 16-19 state "Every {{key}} MUST resolve to a value... If ANY placeholder is unresolved -> ERROR, refuse to write" and CLAUDE.md §13 Layer A + migration doc 20260601_anti_fabrication_3layer_system_01.md:45-46 state a fabricated number is "physically impossible." Rendering an un-computed null as the literal 'None' breaks that by-construction guarantee.

Strongest disconfirmation-of-my-skepticism evidence: the sibling renderer .claude/skills/methods-example/tools/render_figure_spec.py — whose own header line 7 says it follows "與專案 scripts/fill_report.py 同模式" — handles this EXACT case explicitly: lines 44-45 raise Refuse when a verified node's `value is None` ("value is null — 先 LOCK-AND-GATHER 落檔真值再渲染", exit 3), with a separate `optional` resolver (lines 50-54) for intentionally-nullable nodes. This proves the project's intent is that null metric values must refuse, and that fill_report.py simply lacks the guard its sibling already implements. So this is not a reviewer misunderstanding — no context makes the current behavior correct.

Downstream-escape claim also confirmed: number_provenance.py extractors _P1/_P2/_P3 (lines 46-53) only match digit-bearing tokens (>=2-decimal floats, AUC=\d.., percentages). 'None'/'nan' contain no digits and match none, so they pass Layer B undetected (even 'AUC=None' fails _P2 which requires \d after '='). No test file exists for fill_report.py (only fill_report.py and number_provenance.py under scripts/tests).

Calibration on severity: requires a data.json with a present key holding null/NaN — plausible and explicitly anticipated (it's the natural JSON serialization of an un-computed Python None, and the sibling tool guards precisely it). A missing key IS correctly caught, and a literal 'None' in a report is more conspicuous to a human than a plausible fake number, which modestly limits real-world damage. But it defeats the foundational "physically impossible to fabricate" invariant the entire Layer A rests on. HIGH stands.
